full_judgment:
10. In the instant case however the question is whether there was any fraud in executing the document as alleged by the plaintiff or just a bonafide mistake without fraud calling for rectification. There is a presumption of good faith in human transaction and therefore he who alleges fraud or bad faith need to prove the same by leading evidence to the satisfaction of the Court as to the existence of a fraud which would invalidate the document itself to the extent of the fraud committed. It is again the settled principle of law that a finding of a court as to the existence of fraud or the non-existence of the same would be a question of fact and not a question of law. It would be a question of law if however it could be shown that in arriving at that conclusion, as to the existence of fraud or mistake of fact, a wrong inference was drawn by a non consideration of the evidence on record or by a misreading of the same, thereby, causing the wrong inference to be drown in coming to a wrong conclusion, as to fact. This could only also be shown by showing that there was a misreading of a document which is a title document, causing a wrong inference. In the instant case the dispute is related to Ext, 4, being the patta, dated 28-2-45 and it is the title document. On a reference to the said patta it is seen that the said document written in Bengali referred to plots no. 1290 of khatian no. 65 and not a plot under khatian no. 66 and the said plot is described to be 1'14 decimals and the nature of the land is described as Bastu. It also includes plot no. 1291 under khatian no.65 covering an area of 1'32 decimals and the nature of the land is described to be Bilan and the total area of the land leased out of those plots, is described to be 2'46 acres of land. Plaintiff claims this plot to be only plot no. 1292 covering an area of 2'86 under khatian no. 66. So appears that the mistake as alleged by the plaintiff would refer not.only to the plot numbers but also to the area involved to a considerable extent. It 4 also change the khatian because plot no. 1290 a 1291 stands in khatian no. 65 and the area of the 2 plots in total is recorded in that khatian to he 2.55 decimals where according to the plaintiff plot 1292 would cover 2.86 acres. This is not a mistake of minor description but this is a mistake which in total in nature specially in view of the allegation I made by the plaintiff that plot no. 1290 and 1291 could not be taken from the defendant because those were their own properties from before the lease of their own property. This was not, thus. a mistake of fact as to description but a deliberate fraud committed by the defendant while inserting the plots already belonging to the plaintiff.. 

 13. It is not a case of adverse possession and none fought out the suit on such an issue. Further, though an entry in khatian is not an evidence of title, it would be a prima facie evidence of possession. Possession is so recorded in the Government record in the name of defendant No. 1. and not in the name of the plaintiff. This the court of the first instance filed to take into consideration, as to the presumption of possession that would arises in favour of the defendant in view of the entry in the S.A. Khatian and the pleader Commissioner report has not rebutted the said presumption in proving, that the plaintiff was in possession of the instant homestead plot to the exclusion of the defendant. Further, a Pleader Commissioner's report is not binding upon the court. It is like any other evidence and need be considered in the light of the circumstances of each case.
